 As an engineer at Notion, you’ll help shape core user experiences and accelerate how people discover value in Notion. You'll tackle meaningful challenges with increasing autonomy, crafting code that millions of users will experience. You'll take ownership of projects that matter, make critical technical decisions, and contribute your unique perspective to our product vision. Working alongside passionate experts across design, product, and data, you'll help shape the future of how people work.
   

  

 We're looking for an New Grad AI Engineer to join as a strategic partner in shaping Notion's AI vision. You'll work on cutting\-edge AI\-powered features, leveraging LLMs, embeddings, and other AI technologies to make Notion more intelligent and capable.
   

  

**Role**
 This role may be aligned to one of multiple AI\-focused teams at Notion. Depending on team match and business needs, you could work on:
   

  

* AI product engineering: building model\-powered features end\-to\-end (UX, APIs, retrieval, orchestration, quality, and reliability)
* Model \& systems engineering: improving model integration and performance (latency, cost, safety, robustness) and building the infrastructure that supports model serving and experimentation
* Evaluation \& quality (evals): creating evaluation frameworks and automated/ human\-in\-the\-loop testing to measure and improve model and product quality


 What You’ll Achieve
   

  

* Partner with your team to prototype and ship an AI\-powered product improvement
* Own a scoped productionization project: integrate a new model/technique into an existing workflow, add monitoring \+ guardrails, or improve latency/cost/reliability.

 Texas Instruments is looking for a Sr. AI/ML engineer who is experienced with developing and deploying AI/ML solutions at scale.  We're seeking a Machine Learning Engineer with solid foundational expertise to develop and deploy intelligent solutions across our smart manufacturing platform. * Generative AI exposure — hands\-on experience with LLMs, prompt engineering, or RAG systems; familiarity with OpenAI, Anthropic, or similar APIs; curiosity about multi\-agent systems
* Database \& data pipeline knowledge — working familiarity with relational and NoSQL databases; experience building or optimizing data pipelines; understanding of structured vs. unstructured data handling
* Software engineering practices — proficiency with Git/GitHub, JIRA, issue tracking; ability to write clean, testable Python code; familiarity with agile development and CI/CD concepts


**Preferred Requirements**
* Smart Manufacturing— prior work with IoT, manufacturing execution systems (MES), or connected factory environments
* Advanced AI/ML capabilities — experience building with LLMs or generative AI APIs; familiar with prompt engineering and AI workflow optimization
* Manufacturing or industrial domain exposure — familiarity with manufacturing environments, IoT systems, or operational processes; any exposure to semiconductor or discrete manufacturing
* Production ML experience — experience deploying models to production; understanding of model versioning, monitoring, or retraining pipelines
* DevOps \& containerization — hands\-on experience with Docker, Kubernetes, or cloud deployment (AWS, GCP, Azure); basic CI/CD pipeline knowledge
* Multi\-agent or advanced GenAI projects — exposure to agent frameworks, LangChain, or similar tools; experience with more complex LLM workflows beyond single\-turn prompts

**About Pelico**
 Every 16 minutes, something disrupts how a factory runs. Supply chains don't fail from bad decisions, they fail from late ones. Pelico's platform already helps leading manufacturers anticipate and respond to blockers. Multiple AI agents are already deployed on top of the platform to drive outcomes everyday.
   

  

 The next leap: an agentic orchestration platform that lets outside companies (manufacturers \& partners) autonomously build and deploy their own agents. You would be a founding engineer building it \- hands\-on from day one, with flagship manufacturers as design partners to prove it with.
   

  

**About The Role**
 Companies have multiple founding moments and Pelico is going through a new one.
   

  

 You would be one of the founding engineers of our new agentic platform, building alongside a small, super talented, high\-bar team. This is a hands\-on seat from day one: you write the code that manufacturers and their own AI teams build on, close to real customers and real factory data.
   

  

 You benefit from company assets (data, events dependency graphs, simulation engine, next best action algorithms) and the reach that comes from Pelico running the operational data of multiple leading manufacturers.
   

  

****What You'll Do****
* Ship agent capabilities end to end. Build real features from the tool/MCP and orchestration backend through to the React console, live for users \- not demos.
* Harden the runtime. Durable execution, retries, scheduling, and human\-in\-the\-loop approvals on agent actions that carry real consequences.
* Make agents trustworthy. Grow the eval harness (scenario evals, LLM\-as\-judge) so we catch regressions in agent behavior before they ship.
* Build a console people believe. Real\-time streaming of agent events, tool calls, and approvals \- clear, fast, and reliable enough that a controller trusts it.
* Set a craft bar. Write specs others build against, keep the frontend/backend contract honest, and leave reusable patterns the team adopts.


**About You**
 We care about how good you are and how far you can go, and we calibrate to the experience you bring. This seat is built for exceptional people \- whether you are just out of a top program or already have a few years of serious building behind you.
   

  

* An excellent engineer who ships. You write excellent code and have built real things, full\-stack across a Python backend and a React frontend \- or you are clearly able to get there fast.
* Hungry and driven. You want a hard problem to own, not a comfortable seat, and you have the ceiling to grow into far more.
* Rigorous with non\-deterministic systems. You spec and eval before shipping, trust evidence over vibes, and own what goes out \- including AI\-assisted code \- following problems into production.
* AI\-native and curious. You understand how agent frameworks, tools, and evals actually work under the hood, and you build with AI coding tools every day.
* Calm in fast\-moving ambiguity. You stay effective on a stack where this quarter's best practice changes next quarter, turning uncertainty into a workable plan.


*Nice to have: real AI/agent product experience (MCP, agent frameworks, evals); durable workflow engines (e.g. Temporal); streaming UIs; observability (OpenTelemetry); spec\-driven development; multi\-tenant SaaS, or aerospace/defense/discrete\-manufacturing context.*
****Why Pelico****
 If You Want To Build Something Hard From The Ground Up, With Real Ownership From Day One, This Is The Seat. What Comes With It
   

  

* A founding team and a real mandate. You help build Condor from its early days, with genuine ownership of what you ship and room to grow fast.
* The highest\-stakes work you could take on. You build for some of the largest manufacturers, at the scale of their global operations, on a moat competitors cannot copy: we own both the factory simulation and the scoreboard that says whether an agent actually helped.
* A small, elite, AI\-native team. Be challenged by strong peers, learn quickly, and ship fast.
* Competitive salary benchmarked to your market, plus health, dental, and vision coverage and a learning budget.

Who We Are
   

  

 Notion is the collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents think together. We're building one place where your knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools live side by side, so work is faster, clearer, and less fragmented. Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion.
   

  

 Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. Our goal isn’t to ship the next feature. Each and every team of Notinos is working to set the standard for how humans work together in the AI era. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work.
   

  

**About The Role**
 Notion is looking for an experienced engineer who has designed and built secure software systems to help define the security foundations for our AI products. You’ll work with product and engineering teams on agent runtimes, tool permissions, retrieval, content writes, observability, and abuse\-resistant design. You’ll turn product risks into clear architecture, reusable guardrails, automated tests, and production systems that help teams ship new features safely.
   

  

 This role is based in San Francisco. We work from our offices on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays (our Anchor Days) because we do our best thinking and building together in person. We’re looking for someone who’s excited to work alongside the team during those days.
   

  

**What You'll Achieve**
* Define and build security architecture for product surfaces that operate across customer workspace content, including tool execution, content writes, retrieval, permission checks, provenance, and auditability.
* Make the secure path the easy path for product teams by shipping reusable libraries, review patterns, test fixtures, and guardrails that prevent classes of vulnerabilities.
* Build automated red\-team and regression testing for risks such as prompt injection, indirect instruction following, data exfiltration, tool misuse, cross\-tenant leakage, and unsafe workspace mutations.
* Translate threat models for new product surfaces into concrete engineering requirements, production checks, and launch criteria.
* Use production signals, incident learnings, and targeted experiments to harden Notion over time, then feed those learnings back into architecture and developer workflows.
* Help define the security bar for how engineers use coding agents, MCP\-enabled tools, hooks, and internal automation without introducing new risk.


**Skills You'll Need To Bring**
* Secure software engineering craft: You have 8\-10\+ years of experience designing, building, or securing complex software systems, and you are comfortable working in production code with product and platform engineers.
* Security architecture judgment: You can look at a complex system and reason about where the permissions, data flow, or trust boundaries are likely to get weird, and help re\-design it to make them better.
* Security product strategy: You can turn a complex security risk you see into a product design or architecture that can be built.
* Builder mindset: You’d rather leave behind a useful tool, test, library, or pattern than a task or project for someone else to pick up later.


**Nice To Haves**
* Experience building or securing products with tool use, retrieval, workflow automation, content writes, or complex permission boundaries.
* Hands\-on experience with prompt\-injection testing, red teaming, model behavior evaluation, or abuse\-resistant application design.
* Experience with enterprise SaaS security models: permissions, sharing, audit logs, data residency, encryption, compliance, or customer\-facing trust guarantees.
* Experience building developer tooling, CI checks, coding\-agent workflows, MCP integrations, or internal frameworks that shape how engineers build software.
* Public security research, vulnerability writeups, conference talks, or open\-source work related to product security or secure developer infrastructure.

Founding Data Scientist: Measurement, Psychometrics \& the FSU Career Profile Future State University (FSU)
 



  





 About FSU We're building an AI\-native applied learning platform: a 3D simulation engine that converts any syllabus or training doc into immersive, decision\-based career simulations. Fortnite\-meets\-LinkedIn for education. But under the hood, FSU is a measurement system that happens to run as a game. Every decision a learner makes inside a sim becomes scored, traceable evidence of what they can actually do, and that evidence rolls up into the FSU Career Profile: a new kind of resume, built from behavior, not test scores.
 



  





 The Role We're hiring a Founding Data Scientist to own that measurement system end to end. You are equal parts measurement scientist and data/ML engineer: you build the models that turn behavior into scores, and you prove those scores are valid. This is the person who makes FSU's core claim true, that a number on a Career Profile means what we say it means, and would survive a skeptical psychometrician.
 



  





 This is hands\-on and foundational. You will design the scoring architecture, build the evidence pipeline, validate it against real psychometric standards, co\-validate it with our academic research partners, and stand up the dashboards that make all of it legible to students, instructors, and us. You build the measurement, and you build the system that produces it.
 



 If you've built assessment or scoring models, you think in constructs, validity, and reliability, and you can ship the engineering yourself, read on.
 



  





 What You'll Own
 


* The scoring architecture: an evidence\-centered design pipeline (Mislevy\-style) that turns every gradeable moment into typed, routed, provenance\-backed evidence. The append\-only event spine and the per\-learner mastery model that is the single source of truth for every score.
* Validity and reliability: content validity by construction (constructs anchored to learning objectives), discriminant validity (proving our dimensions measure distinct things, not the same thing five times), and inter\-rater reliability between our LLM raters and human experts. You own the evidence that our measurement holds up.
* Knowledge tracing: per\-concept mastery estimation (BKT and beyond) from decisions graded against authored answer keys.
* Behavioral measurement: estimating durable skills, professional identity, values, and epistemology from behavior in simulations, each with confidence, recency, and a traceable chain back to the exact moment that produced the number.
* The FSU Career Profile: the read model behind our credential. You turn the mastery model into the profile employers and learners trust, verified by doing, with provenance behind every claim.
* LLM\-as\-rater systems: rubric design, prompt versioning, eval sets, and the stability and audit tooling that keeps a model\-graded score defensible.
* Internal analytics for all three audiences: student engagement and at\-risk detection, instructor class\-insight dashboards, and an internal observability and watchdog view (latency, errors, cost\-per\-session, model drift) across the full stack.
* Co\-validation with our academic partners: working alongside published researchers to independently validate the instrument.
* Recruiting, mentoring, and building the data team beneath you as we scale.



  





 What You Bring
 


* Serious data science and ML engineering chops. You build production models in Python and ship them; you are not just analyzing in a notebook.
* Real grounding in measurement: psychometrics, educational measurement, or assessment science. Validity, reliability, construct modeling, IRT, BKT, or evidence\-centered design. You have built something that had to measure a person fairly.
* Fluency with LLMs as measurement instruments: eval design, LLM\-as\-judge, and the discipline to know when a model's score is trustworthy and when it isn't.
* Enough full\-stack range to stand up your own dashboards and wire read models into a product. You don't wait on someone else to make your work visible.
* Startup\-native: hands\-on, fast, and comfortable owning an ambiguous, foundational problem from scratch.
* Clear thinking about data. You know the difference between pulling a number and knowing whether it's any good, and you can explain a validity argument to someone who isn't a statistician.



  





 Bonus
 


* Published or applied work in educational measurement, learning analytics, or game\-based assessment.
* Knowledge tracing, IRT, or Bayesian modeling in production.
* Simulation, serious\-games, or EdTech background.
* MongoDB, LangChain / LangSmith, or LLM\-eval tooling in your stack.
* You've built a credential, a score, or a rating that other people relied on to make real decisions.



  





 Why Join FSU Own the measurement system behind a genuinely new credential, the thing that decides whether "verified by doing" is real or just marketing. This is a rare problem: measuring what people can actually do, from behavior, with the rigor to defend it and the AI tooling to do it at scale. Greenfield architecture, real academic co\-validation, high equity, real ownership, and a world\-class mission\-driven team.
 



  





 🚀 See FSU in action: 🎮 Trailer: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v\=H\_i2L7BXH5A
 



 How to Apply Send your resume and a short note on the hardest measurement or scoring problem you've owned: how you built it, and how you knew it was valid. Email team@futurestateuniversity.com.
 



  





 Lawrence Bugg Founder \& CEO, Future State University
